To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cocaine-preferring individual rats have an increased proportion of cocaine use-coding OFC neurons that progressively fire more than other action coding OFC neurons few seconds before cocaine use is actually chosen.

cocaine use and nondrug actions are encoded by nonoverlapping OFC neuronal populations that compete during action selection and that a population size bias in favor of cocaine neurons represents the preference for cocaine use.
the orbitofrontal (OFC) cortex represents individual preferences by a population size difference that systematically favors the preferred action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain encodes individual preferences for drug use and with how this preference is translated into action.
the mechanisms that explain individual differences in drug use.
the neural mechanisms underlying individual differences in the preference for a drug (cocaine) over a nondrug (food) action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the orbitofrontal cortical circuitry that controls action selection is biased toward cocaine in cocaine-preferrers.
a preference for cocaine use is represented in the orbitofrontal (OF) cortex by an increased proportion of cocaine use-coding OF neurons.
the orbitofrontal prefrontal cortex (OFPFC) is involved in the selection of cocaine use over nondrug-related action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cocaine-preferring individual is one whose orbitofrontal (OFC) neurons encode a larger proportion of cocaine use than of alternative nondrug actions.
cocaine addiction is represented in the orbitofrontal (OFC) cortex by an increased relative size of the population of OFC neurons that encode cocaine use.
the OFC represents individual preference for cocaine in a way that is similar to how the OFC represents the preference for a particular food.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the orbitofrontal prefrontal cortex is a key brain area that encodes an individual preference to use cocaine over other nondrug-related actions.
the orbitofrontal (OF) cortex, a key region for decision-making, represents individual preferences for drug use by a bias in the relative size of drug-related neuronal population.
the orbitofrontal (OFC) cortex is a brain region in the frontal lobe of the brain that is involved in the representation and processing of reward and value.
